title: Homemade Blueberry Compote
excerpt: Make a smooth, glossy compote with the natural sweetness of our blueberries and a subtle touch of lemon. It is the perfect accompaniment for your favorite breakfasts and desserts.
imageAlt: Deep purple blueberry compote in a rustic glass jar, with whole berries suspended in a glossy syrup and a wooden spoon beside it.

ingredients.text: 1 tablespoon grated panela (unrefined cane sugar) or bee honey

steps: Place the Fresh Pick blueberries in a small pot together with the two tablespoons of water, the lemon juice and the grated panela. We use half the usual sweetener because Fresh Pick blueberries have more natural sugar.
Bring the pot to medium heat and stir gently with a wooden spoon to combine the ingredients as the panela dissolves.
Cook for about 10 minutes. You will see how these high-mountain blueberries, so carefully grown in Guasca, begin to release their natural juices and turn the mixture into a deep violet syrup.
With the back of the spoon, gently press half of the blueberries against the side of the pot to release their pulp, leaving the other half whole for a delicious rustic texture.
Add the ground cinnamon if you want an aromatic touch, reduce the heat to the minimum and let it thicken for 3 to 5 more minutes, stirring constantly so it doesn’t stick.
Remove from the heat and let it rest at room temperature for 10 minutes. You will notice that as it cools it takes on a much denser, silkier consistency.
tips: To keep its natural flavor intact, pour the compote into a sterilized glass jar with an airtight lid and keep it refrigerated. It will stay perfect for up to two weeks.
Thanks to the natural sweetness of our blueberries, which naturally reach up to 15° Brix, you don’t need to add refined sugars to get a delicious compote.
Try it warm over a slice of grilled farmer’s cheese or use it to top an ice-cold dessert; the contrast of temperatures and flavors is spectacular.
This recipe uses half the usual sweetener: Fresh Pick blueberries have more natural sugar, so we cut it back. Taste it and, if you prefer it sweeter, add a little more.
